name: Hezron
overview: Hezron was a male member of the tribe of Reuben, uniquely identified as the son of Reuben. He is listed among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational genealogy of the Israelite people. His descendants, known as the Hezronites, are noted in the biblical census records, indicating a distinct family line within the tribe of Reuben.
namesAndTitles: The name Hezron means "enclosure," a proper name recorded in Genesis 46:9. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaning that may reflect a sense of protection or boundary.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hezron as the son of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. No additional family relationships are listed beyond this direct paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Hezron's significance lies in his place within the genealogy of Israel as a son of Reuben, contributing to the lineage that entered Egypt during the patriarchal migration. The mention of the Hezronites in the census of Numbers underscores the enduring legacy of his family line within the tribe of Reuben. His inclusion in these genealogical records helps establish the continuity of God's covenant people through successive generations.
